newsitem.title: USA: Cablevision launches Internet cable access.
newsitem.headline: Cablevision launches Internet cable access.

text.p: Cablevision System Corp said on Tuesday it has started the commercial rollout of its high-speed service that uses cable wires to connect personal computers directly with the Internet and online computer services.

The company said its new service, Optimum Online, is now available to 15,000 homes in Oyster Bay, N.Y., and should be expanded to more than 150,000 subscribers in Long Island, N.Y., and Connecticut in 1997.

For unlimited access to the Internet and other services customers will pay either a monthly charge of $34.95 when users buy a cable modem for $295 or $44.95 per month with the modem included. Also there is a one-time installation fee of $150, reduced temporarily to $100.

Using coaxial cable allows customers to communicate and download information 50 times faster than they can over telephone wires, Cablevision said. Customers also will not have to pay for a second telephone line.

"Our goal is to offer our customers a broad range of services over Cablevision's network. Optimum Online is a fantastic step in providing them access to that world of information, delivered at exceptional speed," said James Dolan, Cablevision's chief executive.
Customers will be able to access proprietary local content, movie and television listings and download full-motion video in addition to the Internet offerings.
